correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact theorem on p in (0,1), tau>0: the inverse branches of Bernoulli KL divergence give u(s),v(s), r=v/u in ((1-p)/p,1) for p>1/2. Differentiating R_r(w)=r^2(A+Bw-w^2)/(A-Brw-r^2w^2) yields r^2(1+r)J_r/(...)^2; J_r>=J_{(1-p)/p}=B(1-p)(p-w)^2/p>0. The ratio of equal-energy displacements decreases strictly, and the log-odds beta density is an e^{-tau s} tilt of branch weights with decreasing conditional k(s)=r/(1+r). Monotone likelihood-ratio of the energy tilt proves the strict CDF trend. Escape to infinite energy for tau down to 0 and concentration at zero for tau to infinity give limits 1-p and 1/2. Reflecting p handles p<1/2. The beta-binomial identity with parameters ((n-1)t,t), cutoff (n-1)/n, gives the exact discrete strictness and infimum; n=2 is symmetric. Independently checked the symbolic derivative identity using SymPy and several rational binomial sequences using Fraction; finite tests supplement the analytic argument.
